title: South China Sea Code of Conduct: A Deal Is Not Enough
author: Abdul Rahman Yaacob
text:
Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi delivers a speech on China-ASEAN relations at the ASEAN Secretariat in Jakarta, Indonesia, on July 11, 2022.
Credit: ASEAN Secretariat/Kusuma Pandu Wijaya
As ASEAN and China work toward concluding a Code of Conduct (COC) for the South China Sea in 2026, the central question is not simply whether an agreement can be reached, but whether it will meaningfully reduce tensions. A deal is not enough if it does not address the underlying drivers of tension and shape actors’ behaviors. The South China Sea is a contested maritime zone, involving China and ASEAN members Brunei, Malaysia, the Philippines, and Vietnam. To address the overlapping maritime claims and disputes, ASEAN and China have been negotiating a COC to establish a rules-based framework to manage maritime disputes, reduce miscalculations, and prevent armed conflict. [...]
